verses.verse:
आंदोलन च वक्रत्वं अभ्यासः स्वर संगति।
विकर्षणं श्रुतीनां चेत्येते पंच किृया मताः।११९।
verses.text: Āndolana (oscillation), vakratva (crookedness), abhyāsa (repetition), svara-saṅgati (association of notes) and vikarṣaṇa (pulling) of the śrutis: these are held to be the five actions.

commentary.text: In the svara-vistāra (elaboration of notes) of rāgas, five actions are done besides the tāna elements. Their names are given in the śloka above. 1 Āndolana (oscillation), that is, making the blowing breath tremble on the note on which one pauses. This āndolana is mostly done on the guitar. On the bansī (bamboo flute) some people are not able to do it, because for that it is necessary for the sādhaka (practitioner) to practise bhastrikā prāṇāyāma (breath control) for 6 months in the winters. When we take the breath in and out quickly, just as a dog sits and pants in the hot days, that kind of practice is called bhastrikā prāṇāyāma. It should be done for two or three minutes every day. 2 Vakratva (crookedness): when we do not sound a note straight, but use it joined with the notes around it, we show a changed form, sometimes with one sparśa (touch) and sometimes with many sparśas, that is, in the form of mirkīs - this we call a saṃyukta svara (joined note) or vakra svara (crooked note). In other śāstras there is a somewhat different definition of vakra, but by that the crookedness of the rāga becomes clear, not that of the note. 3 Abhyāsa (repetition) means repeating the rāga-identifying note group. 4 Vikarṣaṇa (pulling) means drawing the śrutis in between, in the form of mīṇḍ (glide), to go from one note to another. 5 Svara-saṅgati (association of notes) means using, besides the vādī and saṃvādī, the association of some [other] notes that suits the rāga.
